subject.title: Discord: make native command visibility follow account/channel routing

question: Which Discord native command visibility policy should OpenClaw support for multi-account setups where account/channel routing already exists?
rationale: Current source confirms execution-only authorization, but permission syncing, guild-scoped deployment, explicit reconcile/config controls, and namespacing have different Discord API, upgrade, and operator-control tradeoffs.

options.title: Derive Visibility From Routing
options.body: Use configured Discord account/guild/channel routing as the desired command-visibility source after validating Discord permission semantics and cache propagation behavior.

options.title: Add Explicit Operator Controls
options.body: Provide a CLI or config-controlled reconciliation path so operators choose which accounts expose generic commands and when Discord permissions are rewritten.

options.title: Document Manual Discord Setup
options.body: Keep OpenClaw execution auth unchanged and document manual Discord app permission setup as the supported multi-account visibility workflow.

recommendation.title: Derive Visibility From Routing
recommendation.body: Use configured Discord account/guild/channel routing as the desired command-visibility source after validating Discord permission semantics and cache propagation behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history for Discord deploy behavior and the documented current visibility contract points to steipete.
